title: One Earthquake Shifted Earth's Axis 6.5 Inches and Shortened the Day

scenes.text: One earthquake shortened every day on Earth.
On March 11th, 2011, a magnitude nine earthquake hit Japan.
NASA scientists calculated it cut the day by about one point eight millionths of a second.
It also shifted Earth's axis by about six and a half inches.
And Japan itself became about thirteen feet wider.
One quake, and the whole planet spins a tiny bit faster.

description:
The 2011 magnitude 9 earthquake in Japan may have shortened each day by about 1.8 microseconds, according to NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
It also shifted Earth's figure axis by about 6.5 inches.
What other force do you think could change the whole planet's spin? Comment below.
first_comment: One earthquake moved the whole planet's axis. What natural event do you think is the most powerful?
